Paleomagnetics of Ringerike Old Red Sandstone and related
rocks, southern Norway: implications for pre-Carboniferous
separation of Baltica and British terranes
D.N. DOUGLASS
Department of Earth Sciences, Dartmouth College, Hanover, NH 03755 (U.S.A.) *
(Received December 1,1986; revised version accepted August 11,1987)
Abstract
Douglass, D.N., 1988. Paleomagnetics of Ringerike Old Red Sandstone and related rocks, southern Norway:
implications for pre-Carboniferous separation of Baltica and British terranes. Tectonophysics, 148:11-27.
Paleomagnetic study of two stratigraphic sections of the Upper Silurian-Lower Devonian Ringerike Sandstone, Oslo
area, Norway, indicate a straightforward multicomponent NRM for these rocks. A lower temperature magnetization
component gives a southwest and up (reversed polarity) in-situ direction, yields a negative fold test (i.e.
post-folding) at the 99% confidence level, and is nearly identical to directions obtained from overlying Permo-
Carboniferous lavas. A high temperature magnetization component exhibits both normal and reversed polarity
directions, passes a fold test at the 95% confidence level, and is supported by a baked contact test which indicates a
pre-intrusion age of magnetization. This characteristic high temperature component was successfully isolated in 79
samples, from 19 sites within the Ringerike succession. Results indicate a tilt corrected, characteristic magnetic
direction of declination = 26 O, inclination = - 16 O, which is consistent with earlier work. This direction corre-
sponds to a time-integrated paleopole position of 19ON latitude, 164” longitude (dp = 4.8”, dm = 9.3O). When
compared to previous results from rocks of similar age from the British Isles, an approximately 20° latitudinal
displacement between Britain and Baltica during Late Silurian-Early Devonian time is suggested.
Introduction pieces of Euramerica could have still existed.
Therefore, paleomagnetic evidence of this age
